Thanks Soojin — attached our updated demand note (we merged internal product usage projections into your CSV).

Short answers to your questions:
- Primary production model will be a T5-derived family with 16k context for now; we expect to trial 32k on a small portion of traffic in September. No fp32 requirement at launch.
- Ramp cadence: pilot mid-September (10% traffic), EU + additional US scale in Nov -> December full production.

1) Can you outline the minimum reserved slot commitment (GPU-hours/week) to guarantee our target p95 latency at 16k context?
2) If we need to burst beyond reserved in Nov/Dec, what's your standard lead time for additional reserved slots vs on-demand burst?

Thanks — I can join the call at 11:30 PT on Friday.

Amelia / team — quick infra readout ahead of the bridge.

TL;DR: For a 16k-context T5-family workload at your target p95, we recommend reserving a baseline equivalent to 8 dedicated A100-class GPUs (continuous) with a planned burst pool of +4 GPUs in the Nov/Dec window. That baseline keeps p95 under 400ms under your current traffic shape.

Notes and constraints:
- Lead time for increasing reserved capacity in our Dedicated product is typically 6–8 weeks for committed slots (procurement + provisioning). We can provide 2–3 week short-term burst capacity in most regions but that comes at on-demand pricing and is subject to pool availability.
- If the 32k trial expands beyond 10% traffic, we should plan a temporary model-variant strategy: quantize/half the model for latency-sensitive paths and route heavy-context requests to a small, higher-cost pool. That avoids a 2x slot increase.
- We flagged a potential contention on the east-us burst pool between late-Nov and mid-Dec due to holidays + planned infra upgrades. Recommend early procurement for that period if you need guaranteed headroom.

I've attached a simple capacity runbook and the capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx with the numbers filled in for the suggested baseline.

Ben
